# The catalogue loads in stages, and "not yet computed" is a separate list

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-staged-catalogue-loading`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

`load_catalogue()` is one synchronous call: it walks the source roots, evaluates every `gear.gdl`,
parses every gear crate and every SDK crate, joins contracts and plugins, and only then returns.
That is the right shape for a CLI, which has nothing to show until it has everything.

It is the wrong shape for the Studio. The Catalogue widget renders a tree of gears by category with
capability badges and co-location chips, and it cannot wait: **the data arrives at very different
costs.** A description is a few hundred bytes of Starlark; a gear's crate is a syn parse of every
`.rs` under `src/`.

Measured on the 14-gear slice: 255 `.rs` files parsed, ~0.7 s. `gears/` in `gears-rust` holds
**2658** `.rs` files, so a full registry is roughly ten times that — seconds of blocking before the
first row appears, growing with the tree.

Two questions follow, and the second is the harder one. How is the load staged? And how does a
consumer tell "this gear exposes no GTS types" from "nobody has looked yet"? Today both are an empty
`Vec`.

## Decision Drivers

* Time to the first rendered row must not scale with the size of the tree.
* A consumer that forgets to check for incompleteness must not be able to render a confident wrong
  answer. This project has already found three facts that were quietly wrong because something
  looked complete and was not: `has_extension_point` in `gear.toml`, a provider's transports, and a
  plugin's GTS types.
* The IR is shared with TypeScript through `ts-rs`, so a change in shape reaches every binding and
  every consumer.
* Whatever is decided must not make the CLI's single-shot path worse; it is the reproducibility
  surface and it wants everything.

## Considered Options

* **A — a separate `pending` list.** `Catalogue.gears` keeps its meaning: fully projected gears. A
  `pending: Vec<PendingGear>` alongside carries what is discovered or declared but not finished.
* **B — a `stage` field on `GearDescriptor`.** Every gear is in the catalogue from the moment it is
  discovered, carrying how far it got.
* **C — tri-state fields.** `Known(T) | Absent | Pending` on every field that a later stage fills.

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen: A, a separate `pending` list.**

`Option::None` and an empty `Vec` keep exactly one meaning — *absent* — everywhere in the IR. A
gear present in `catalogue.gears` is complete and can be read without qualification; a gear that is
not there yet is in `pending`, where the only fields available are the ones that are genuinely
known.

### The five stages

| stage | work | what it yields | cost on the slice |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0** discover | one walk per source root for `gear.gdl` | paths only | one walk |
| **S1** declare | evaluate each description (Starlark, tiny files); locate documents (`stat` only) | `display_name`, `description`, `category`, `visibility`, the `package`/`sdk` locators, `requires`, `serves`, `cluster_plugins`, `docs` | milliseconds per file |
| **S2** project gear | `syn` over the gear crate's `src/` | `id`, `runtime_caps`, `colocated_deps`, `lifecycle`, `client_trait`, `fills`, a provider's transports | **165 files** |
| **S3** project sdk | `syn` over the SDK crates | contracts, extension points, GTS types, vendor defaults | 90 files, **crates shared between gears** |
| **S4** join | contract merge, plugin resolution | `GBX0206`, `GBX0511`-`GBX0517` | cheap, but needs S2+S3 of the gears involved |

### The consequence that shapes the surface

**`GearId` is projected, so it does not exist until S2.** At S1 there is a name to display and no
identifier to key by. A tree rendered at S1 must therefore be keyed by `gdl_path`, and the `id`
arrives later to join against.

This is a direct consequence of ADR `cpt-gearbox-adr-macro-projected-catalogue` that the ADR itself
does not state. It is also what turns staged loading from an improvement into a requirement: an
implementation that keys its tree by `id` has no choice but to block until every crate is parsed.

```rust
/// A gear discovered and declared, but not yet projected.
///
/// Keyed by `gdl_path` rather than `GearId` because the id is projected from
/// Rust and does not exist at this stage.
pub struct PendingGear {
    pub source: SourceId,
    pub gdl_path: RelPath,
    pub stage: LoadStage,               // Discovered | Declared
    pub display_name: Option<String>,   // from S1
    pub category: Option<String>,       // from S1
    pub description: Option<String>,
}
```

### Consequences

* **Clicking a pending row must still work.** The path to `gear.gdl` is known from S0, so "reveal the
  description" is available before anything is parsed. A pending row that does nothing on click would
  be a worse experience than a slow one.
* **The tree's grouping is available early and its badges are not.** `category` is declared (S1);
  `runtime_caps` and `colocated_deps` are projected (S2). So the shape of the tree settles first and
  fills in — which is the desirable order, and not something the widget has to work for.
* **Parsing each crate once per load becomes a precondition, not an optimisation.** A staged loader
  that re-parses shared crates cannot be cheap however it is scheduled. Measured on the slice before
  the cache: `tenant-resolver-sdk` was read four times (host plus three plugins) and
  `authn-resolver-sdk` three. With the cache, the same load parses **19 crates for 25 requests**.
* **The CLI keeps its single-shot path and gains one observable.** `gearbox catalogue --format text`
  now reports crates parsed against requests, which is the only externally visible sign the cache
  exists — the catalogue itself is byte-identical either way.
* **`pending` must be empty when a load completes.** Otherwise the list becomes a place where gears
  quietly go missing, which is the failure mode `Option` was protected from in the first place.
* The staged engine API, its progress callback and any parallelism are deferred to M8, with the RPC
  surface. The shape of a progress callback is determined by what `$/progress` actually needs, and
  there is nowhere to check its value before then. The workspace deliberately has no parallelism
  dependency yet.

### Confirmation

* `crates/gearbox-engine/tests/scans.rs` — sharing happens (requests exceed distinct crates by at
  least five), no gear loses its crate to a key collision, and two loads of the same tree agree
  byte-for-byte including both counters.
* The catalogue's JSON hash is unchanged by the cache; that equality is the point of the change and
  was checked before and after.
* `cpt-gearbox-nfr-first-paint` and `cpt-gearbox-fr-incremental-catalogue` in the PRD carry the
  requirement; the stage table above is the shared reference for both.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A — a separate `pending` list

* Good, because `Option::None` and an empty `Vec` keep one meaning across roughly forty fields.
* Good, because a consumer that ignores `pending` renders fewer gears — visibly incomplete — rather
  than a confident wrong answer about a gear it did render.
* Good, because the CLI can ignore it entirely: a completed load has an empty `pending`.
* Bad, because the editor has to merge two collections to render one tree, and a gear moves between
  them as it completes.

### B — a `stage` field on `GearDescriptor`

* Good, because one collection means the UI renders one list and re-renders in place.
* Bad, and decisively: every consumer must check `stage` before reading any projected field, and a
  forgotten check produces a confident wrong answer. That is the exact failure this project has
  already hit three times, and the type system would not help once.
* Bad, because "a gear in the catalogue" would stop meaning "a gear we understand".

### C — tri-state fields

* Good, because it is the most precise: each field says whether it is known.
* Bad, because it touches roughly forty fields, every `ts-rs` binding, and every consumer, for
  precision only the loading path needs.
* Bad, because it makes every read site handle a case that is impossible in the CLI.

## More Information

The cache is keyed by canonical path, which is what makes the sharing work at all: the same SDK
reached from a host and from one of its plugins arrives as two different relative paths. Failures are
cached too, so a crate with no `src/` is reported once rather than once per gear that names it.

`Arc<[RustFile]>` rather than `Arc<Vec<RustFile>>`: one allocation instead of two, and it derefs
straight to the `&[RustFile]` every consumer already takes, so no downstream signature changed.

### The decision now has a consumer, and it held

This ADR was written before anything rendered a catalogue, which made it an untested design. The
Theia Catalogue widget is now that consumer, and
`ide/tests/conformance/adr-0009-staged-loading.spec.ts` checks the claim as a timeline rather than as
a final state -- a snapshot after loading would pass even if the tree had appeared all at once. The
sampler is installed before the document has scripts, so it observes a window in which rows are on
screen, named and grouped by category, and still `pending`. When the load is too short to have been
observed at all, the test reports "not observed" rather than passing, because a sampling rate is not
evidence.

One claim in this ADR had no test until that suite existed, and it is the one the widget depends on
most: **the selection survives the pending-to-projected replacement.** Rows are keyed by
`(source, gdl_path)` precisely so that choosing a gear before it is parsed does not lose the choice
when it finishes, and an id-keyed selection could not do that, since the id does not exist at S1.

One thing was learned that the ADR did not anticipate. `gdl_path` is load-bearing beyond keying
rows: the widget keys its **selection** by it as well, so choosing a gear before it is parsed does
not lose the choice when projection replaces the row. A selection keyed by `GearId` could not work
at all, for the same reason the tree cannot be -- the id does not exist until S2.

A second, smaller consequence surfaced in the generated TypeScript. Collection fields carry
`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]`, so `ts-rs` emits them as optional and an empty
collection is not sent at all. On the client, absent and empty are therefore the same value -- which
is the intended reading, and worth stating because it means a client cannot use "field missing" as a
proxy for "not projected yet". `pending` remains the only signal for that.

* Depends on: ADR `cpt-gearbox-adr-macro-projected-catalogue` — the projected `GearId` is what makes

## Amendment 2026-10-18: bounded parallel source reads

Issue Artifizer/gearbox#5 identifies Windows on-access antivirus latency when
thousands of source files are opened serially. S2/S3 now read sorted source paths
in batches of at most 32 scoped workers. Only text and I/O errors cross threads;
`syn` ASTs and projection stay on the calling thread. At most 32 source texts
are prefetched, bounded by the existing per-file size limit.

The public loader remains synchronous. S0/S1 finish before projection, callbacks
stay on the calling thread, and no event is emitted from a read worker. Files,
parse failures and I/O failures are consumed in sorted order, including when a
later read fails before an earlier parse does. The crate cache and scan counters
are unchanged; cancellation is still observed at the existing event boundaries.
No persistent cache, warm-start protocol or initialize invalidation change is
part of this amendment. Defender exclusions are not required or configured.

Confirmation: `scan::read_tests` covers ordering across multiple batches and
mixed parse/read failures. Existing staged/cancellation/cache tests remain the
behavioral contract. Cold/warm timings with Defender enabled are machine-specific
measurements, not a portable latency guarantee.
